subject: Aroma took me a long time for processing Affy 6.0 data

messages.author: 66ea21dd30af951a
messages.subject: Aroma took me a long time for processing Affy 6.0 data
parts:
Hi,

We are using Aroma to preprocess Cel files for GWA studies. I ran
the following steps. The algorithm works very well except the last
step, which is very very slow. For one plate (about 90 Cel files), the
first two steps can be finished in about half a day. But the last step
has not finished yet after four days running.

Is this expected?


Thanks.


Jerry


Here is the code:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6",
tags="Full")
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf)
si <- getSnpInformation(cdf)
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(plate, cdf=cdf)
acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=verbose)
plm <- AvgCnPlm(csC, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, shift=
+300)
ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm)
fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(ces)
cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)

messages.subject: Re: Aroma took me a long time for processing Affy 6.0 data
parts:
If you had looked through previous discussions then you would see that
there are a number of comments addressing the reason why
aroma.affymetrix takes time to process the data, for example:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/fa28a59394fe8689/600edab654ba6a90?lnk=gst&q=24+hours#600edab654ba6a90
( time for running fit(plm) step)

Plus I believe that you might be missing a step in the above code:
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)

See http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0
for details

regards

Lavinia.

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Aroma took me a long time for processing Affy 6.0 data
parts:
Hi,

as Lavinia says, you've forgot to actually fit() the PLM.

Second, please always report your sessionInfo().

Third, could you please be more specific with what you mean by the
"last step"? Is that

cesN <- process(fln, verbose=verbose)?

If you read the Vignette 'Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)' you
find in the end of Section 'PCR fragment length normalization' the
comment "Fragment-length normalization takes approximately 1
min/array", so "four days" and still running for 90 arrays doesn't
sound right. It could be related to not fitting the PLM, because then
all chip effects are zero and maybe the FLN algorithms doesn't
converge, but that is a bit far fetched.

It would help if you report the verbose output so that we know if
where it "get stuck". I would use

verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8);
timestampOn(verbose);

so that you also get the timing information.

Also, make sure to read the FAQ.

/Henrik

Yes, accessing (reading/writing) data over a shared file system can
slow things down substantially. Alternatively, it is amazing how
clever the cache mechanism on a local drive is and fast the access is
thanks to this.

Please report back on the speedup you get by working towards a local
drive. I think this is of interest to many of us.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.author: 66ea21dd30af951a
messages.subject: Re: Aroma took me a long time for processing Affy 6.0 data
parts:
Sorry I was out of town for several days.

We ran Aroma on a computer cluster powered by Rocks OS. In the cluster
there are 10 computational nodes, 50 cores and a file server. At the
beginning, we submitted one job (one plate, about 90 subjects) into
one core, and so there are about 50 jobs were running at the same
time. Each job has to copy the files from the file server and has to
write CEL files back to the file server. So, the I/O became the
bottleneck of the whole system because for plm fir, about 60% time is
due to I/O. We ran 50 jobs for 10 days and no results came out.

We finally decided that this was due to I/O issue. So, we copied the
files for each job to the local machines and wrote the results to the
local machine too. After all jobs finished, we collected the CEL files
from local drives. Each job took about 15 hours! This is great!


Suggestion:
(1) If you run Aroma in a cluster, we suggest that you let Aroma
access data from local drives instead of file server.
(2) If you run Aroma in a single machine with multiple cores, e.g.
four cores or eight cores, don't be greedy to run four or eight jobs
at the same time. Based on the I/O performance of your computer,
submit at most 2 jobs (based on my experience).


Jerry.
